title: Delete one row
prompt: Delete the trail with id 2. Replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM trails; INSERT INTO trails VALUES (7, 'Birch Walk', 'West', 3.1, 40), (8, 'High Moor', 'East', 12.6, 610), (9, 'Crag Top', 'North', 6.0, 900); INSERT INTO trails VALUES (2, 'Fox Ridge', 'East', 14.0, 870), (3, 'Mill Stream', 'South', 5.2, 90);

title: Remove short trails
prompt: The club is retiring trails shorter than 6 km. Delete them from the trails table. The check looks at the table after your SQL runs, so a SELECT alone won't pass.
hints: Use DELETE FROM with a WHERE clause. Without WHERE, every row is deleted.

check.sql: SELECT id, name FROM trails ORDER BY id;

cases.name: A trail of exactly 6 km
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM trails; INSERT INTO trails VALUES (7, 'Birch Walk', 'West', 3.1, 40), (11, 'Six Mile Lane', 'East', 6.0, 75);

wrongSolutions.why: Also deletes a trail of exactly 6 km
Displays rows without changing the table

title: Never ordered
prompt: Delete customers who have never placed an order. Use EXCEPT inside a subquery to find them.
hints: The subquery lists customer ids except those in orders.

check.sql: SELECT id, name FROM customers ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: DELETE FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM customers EXCEPT SELECT customer_id FROM orders);

wrongSolutions.sql: DELETE FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM customers INTERSECT SELECT customer_id FROM orders);

title: Delete using a list
prompt: Delete employees whose department isn't in the departments table. Keep employees with a NULL department.
hints: NOT IN against departments, which skips NULLs.

check.sql: SELECT id, name, department_id, salary, bonus FROM employees ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET department_id = 99 WHERE id = 13;

solutions: DELETE FROM employees WHERE department_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM departments);

wrongSolutions.sql: DELETE FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NULL;
DELETE FROM employees WHERE department_id IN (SELECT id FROM departments);

title: Fix the join delete
prompt: This uses MySQL's syntax to delete contacts in London. SQLite doesn't support it. Fix it with a simple DELETE.
starterSql:
DELETE c FROM contacts c
WHERE c.city = 'London';
hints: Use just DELETE FROM and WHERE.

check.sql: SELECT id, full_name FROM contacts ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3'); UPDATE contacts SET city = 'London' WHERE id = 12;

title: Keep the first
prompt: Several contacts share a city. Using EXISTS, delete any contact when another contact in the same city has a lower id. Contacts with no city stay.
hints: A correlated subquery compares each row with the others.

check.sql: SELECT id, full_name FROM contacts ORDER BY id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3'); UPDATE contacts SET city = NULL WHERE id = 13; UPDATE contacts SET city = 'Murray' WHERE id = 11;

solutions: DELETE FROM contacts WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM contacts x WHERE x.city = contacts.city AND x.id < contacts.id);

wrongSolutions.sql: DELETE FROM contacts WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM contacts x WHERE x.id < contacts.id);
DELETE FROM contacts WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM contacts x WHERE x.city = contacts.city AND x.id > contacts.id);

title: Keep the top seller per order
prompt: For each order, keep only the item with the highest quantity, breaking ties with the lowest product_id, and delete the other items. The check shows order_items.
hints: Use ROW_NUMBER over rowid in a subquery.

check.sql: SELECT order_id, product_id, quantity FROM order_items ORDER BY order_id, product_id;

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: DELETE FROM order_items WHERE rowid IN (SELECT rowid FROM (SELECT rowid, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY quantity DESC, product_id) AS n FROM order_items) WHERE n > 1);

wrongSolutions.sql: DELETE FROM order_items WHERE rowid IN (SELECT rowid FROM (SELECT rowid, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY quantity, product_id) AS n FROM order_items) WHERE n > 1);
